text.p: A Pennsylvania maker of adhesive tape said it sued Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing Co (3M) Wednesday for allegedly using illegal tactics to wrap up the market.

Pittsburgh-based LePage Inc's said in the suit filed in U.S. District Court for Eastern Pennsylvania that 3M, of St. Paul, Minnesota, "has monopolized or attempted to monopolize the invisible and transparent home and office tape market by squeezing out its small competitors."

The company said 3M engaged in "predatory conduct," such as offering steep discounts to retailers who sold 3M tape exclusively, or selectively offering to LePage's customers private-label products made by 3M.

A spokeswoman for 3M said the company had no immediate comment. "There's nothing we can really say at this point until our attorneys have have had a chance to review the suit," spokeswoman Laura Sutton said.
LePage's said in a release it was seeking $75 million in the suit, representing three times estimated lost profits due to 3M's alleged practices.

LePage's, a privately-held firm, said its share of the $275 million tape market had fallen to around 6-7 percent from 12 percent at the time 3M allegedly began its predatory practices in 1993. Over the same period, profits plummeted from $6.3 million to an operating loss. About 80 percent of the company's annual revenues of about $35 million come from tape sales.
LePage's said it closed one of its tape manufacturing plants, in Winchester, Kentucky, in March. It operates another factory in Gloucester, Massachusetts.
It said 3M holds about a 90 percent share of the market for acetate or cellophane tape.
In its suit, LePage's said 3M had become alarmed at inroads LePage's was making in the market by making private-label tape for major retailers, and in 1993 tried to buy the company.
After talks broke off, 3M began a campaign to drive LePage's from the market, the suit said.
